name: Janus

attributes.attribute: a Roman god with two faces looking in different directions
a month named from Janus, looking to new and old year

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Janus was a Roman god. He had two faces that looked in different directions. His name survives in the month January, which looks both forward to the new year and back to the old. In Celtic lands the Romans met occasional two-faced statues of unnamed gods. They named these after their familiar god Janus. Scholars call such figures Janiform, meaning having the same form as Janus. The original Celtic meaning of the figures is lost. Scholars link them with the reverence for the head as a symbol of essence and power. They also link them with special power given to twins.
objective: Document Janus and the Janiform two-faced statues found in Celtic lands.
key_results: Record Janus and his two faces.
Note his name in the month January.
Explain Janiform statues and their lost meaning.
